meta.notes: Scope: public evidence on Frame.io v4 pain (Premiere/AE marker and comment sync, performance, corporate-network blocking, permissions, presentation), the competitive set, pricing and storage cost. Most pain evidence is Adobe Community threads (2024-2026); Reddit (r/editors, r/premiere) is disallowed by robots.txt for Preuve, so the loudest public complaints could not be cited. help.frame.io, blog.frame.io, Capterra/G2/Trustpilot, PetaPixel and the Blackmagic forum were also unfetchable. Evidence is anecdotal (individual forum posts); no survey or count of affected editors was found. No direct evidence was found for: client corporate IT blocking Frame.io review links specifically (only adjacent cases: an Adobe InDesign review link failing on a corporate network, an org blocking shortened links, uploads failing behind a firewall), lost presentation mode (fxguide instead describes v4's branded Share Builder), slow client playback (only slow panel uploads), or willingness to pay $29/seat (competitors price at $10-25/seat). Contradiction searches: Adobe 25.6 panel rebuild, positive v4 coverage, Frame.io pricing/restricted folders, native Resolve review. Prospects: 17 companies, short of the 20+ target - many boutique editorial sites were image-only, unresolvable or blocked; no fetched page states headcount, so size_estimate is omitted; no company-specific problem evidence was found. Contacts only from companies' own pages; Lightsail's location is cited from a public Denver directory listing. The Frame.io pricing quote comes from the --full fetch of frame.io/pricing.

evidence.statement: A Premiere editor reports that in the Frame.io v4 panel sequence markers no longer upload and markers cannot be synced manually, both of which worked in v3.

evidence.title: FrameIOv4 Bug Hunt/Missing Features (Adobe Community)

evidence.statement: The same editor reports v4 panel uploads are much slower than browser uploads.

evidence.title: FrameIOv4 Bug Hunt/Missing Features (Adobe Community)
evidence.quote: I'm experiencing several bugs in the 'new' v4 panel and like many I regret updating. Shame really as it was a huge selling point and time saver.
evidence.statement: An editor says the Premiere integration was a major selling point and time saver, and regrets updating to v4.

evidence.title: FrameIOv4 Bug Hunt/Missing Features (Adobe Community)
evidence.quote: I'm the Product Manager of the Frame.io integrations into Premiere Pro, and therefore directly responsible for the issues you're seeing. We're aware of a number of these issues
evidence.statement: Adobe's product manager for the Premiere integration publicly acknowledged the marker issues, so the incumbent is actively working on them.

evidence.statement: After upgrading to v4 an editor can no longer export timeline markers as Frame.io comments.

evidence.title: FrameIO seems to be broken (Adobe Community)

evidence.statement: An editor whose clients give notes in Frame.io says v4 broke the notes-to-timeline workflow and they are back to printed notes.

summary.statement: Before v4, the Frame.io Premiere panel imported client comments as timeline markers; editors say v4 stopped markers uploading or syncing and removed the export-markers-as-comments option.
When the integration fails, editors fall back to printed notes or self-made scripts that import comment CSVs as markers.
Resolve users can get reviewer markers straight into the timeline through Blackmagic Cloud Presentations; Vimeo, Dropbox Replay, PageProof and RevCut also offer NLE integrations.
How common each method is among boutiques was not found.

Only adjacent cases were found: an Adobe-hosted review link failing on a corporate network, an organisation that cannot use Frame.io's shortened links for security reasons, and uploads stalling behind a firewall.
One editor built their own review tool because two large clients refused the big platforms over GDPR and AI-training terms.
No evidence on how often client IT blocks Frame.io review links; the frequency is unknown.
Editors describe the broken marker sync as crippling or forcing them back to printouts, but no source quantifies time per project.
Workarounds include printed notes and home-made CSV-to-marker scripts.
Alternatives with NLE integrations are Dropbox Replay, Krock.io, Wipster, Vimeo, PageProof, RevCut and, for Resolve, Blackmagic Cloud Presentations.
Adobe rebuilt the Premiere panel in 25.6 to tie comments to markers, though at least one user still reports markers unusable in 25.6.1.
Frame.io itself already offers restricted folders, no-login share links and branded presentations, so some wedge features are not gaps.
Current per-seat prices: Frame.io $15 (Pro) and $25 (Team) per member per month, Dropbox Replay $10-12 per user, Krock.io $10 per user; RevCut charges EUR 29 per month for four seats.
A small Frame.io tier is bundled with some Creative Cloud subscriptions, and Blackmagic Cloud has a free tier of 20 presentations.
Zero-egress storage such as Cloudflare R2 limits playback bandwidth cost.
No evidence that boutiques would pay $29 per editor seat; market prices sit at $10-25.

current_solutions.statement: Most teams still use Frame.io, which offers no-login client share links and a Premiere panel; v4 broke parts of the marker workflow and Adobe rebuilt the panel in 25.6.
Resolve users have native Blackmagic Cloud Presentations whose markers land in the Resolve timeline, plus third-party plugins (PageProof, RevCut).
Cheaper review tools with NLE integrations exist at about $10 per user per month (Dropbox Replay, Krock.io), and Vimeo also syncs comments into Premiere.
When integrations break, editors fall back to printed notes or home-made scripts that import CSV comments as markers.
